title: Model ingest declaration and runtime sanity checklist
creator: Anna Park
description:
Problem statement: Our current catalog intake fields are inconsistent across community submissions. That ambiguity forces runtime teams to add ad-hoc compatibility fixes and slows safe admission. This ticket defines the minimal immutable declaration that every incoming open model must supply, plus a deterministic runtime sanity checklist that the model onboarding pipeline will run automatically. The goal is to reduce manual triage, reduce rollout surprises, and make automated fallback routing and cost estimation reliable for hosted and dedicated deployments.

Scope clarifications: This work defines requirements only (fields, validation semantics, and test-suite passes). Implementation is out of scope for this ticket and will be tracked separately (ENG followups). We include the expanded set of metadata required for model ingest and the exact pass/fail semantics for the runtime sanity checks that must run in intake and in pre-release canaries.

Non-goals: full model performance benchmarking, customer-facing UI changes, or license legal review beyond a required license field and a simple SPDX check. Detailed quantization guidance and per-accelerator kernel selection are out of scope but should be referenced as notes for follow-up engineering epics.
acceptance_criteria: A clear, minimal JSON schema (flat key set) is defined that every new open-model submission must include; schema file location is referenced in links.
Each schema key has unambiguous semantic text and machine validation rules (type, allowed values, units) documented.

A deterministic runtime sanity checklist is specified with exact test definitions, thresholds, and expected outputs for: tensor layout, tokenizer compatibility, KV-cache behavior, sequence-length handling, and basic generation smoke tests.

Pass/fail semantics for intake: models that fail any critical sanity test are marked as 'blocked' and require manual triage; models that pass all critical tests are eligible for staged admission (canary -> gradual rollout).
Acceptance criteria include explicit fallback signal instructions for the router when a model variant lacks a feature (e.g., no kv-cache => route to variant with cache or use non-streaming path).
Security review required flag is produced automatically for models that declare external weight URLs or non-OSI licenses.
An integration checklist for the onboarding pipeline (CI jobs and artifact checks) is included so Eng can implement automated gates without interpretation gaps.
Product and runtime sign-off owners are named and committed to the gate: Anna Park (PM) and Lucas Moreno (SRE).
tasks: Draft flat ingest declaration schema (minimal required keys) - owner: Ravi Patel
Define deterministic runtime sanity tests and thresholds - owner: Lucas Moreno
Add machine validation rules and example manifests for 3 model families (decoder-only, encoder-decoder, and quantized variants) - owner: Ravi Patel
Document routing fallback signals and expected router behavior - owner: Anna Park
Identify fields requiring security_review_required and draft simple SPDX validation - owner: Priya Singh
Prepare a handoff PRD for Eng implementation that maps schema keys to CI gates and onboarding pipeline steps - owner: Anna Park
decisions: Use a flat declaration schema (no nested objects) to keep validation simpler for CI and to avoid partial reads in the router.
Classify runtime checks into 2 buckets: 'critical' (block admission) and 'advisory' (surface warnings).
Require explicit declared tokenizer name and tokenization test vector (input -> token ids) to prevent token mismatch regressions.
Treat missing kv-cache semantics as advisory for encoder-only models but critical for streaming chat use-cases.
Security flag will be conservative: any external weight URL or non-standard license triggers a security review requirement.
notes: Trade-offs: flat schema simplifies CI but may duplicate fields across variants. We accept duplication to ensure atomic validation per manifest.
Operational impact: SRE must add one new sanity job (quick run on 1x A100 or equivalent) to the intake pipeline; estimated 10m runtime per model.
Rollout plan: start by requiring the declaration for new community model submissions only; backfill existing catalog entries over two quarters prioritized by traffic.
Risks: false positives in runtime smoke tests could block acceptable models. Mitigation: advisory-first approach during the pilot window and human-in-the-loop triage for first 50 submissions.
Follow-ups: ENG epic to wire schema validation to ingestion CI (ENG-XXXXX), and a separate UX ticket to surface warnings in the Console (PM-XXXXX).
